07_outage_costs.yaml.raw_content:
# Outage Cost Parameters
# Expected outage costs based on reliability parameters

outage:
  # Risk growth
  risk_growth_rate: 0.0 # Annual increase in outage rates (>= 0) (default: 0)

  # Capacity at risk factor (φ)
  capacity_at_risk_factor: "auto" # "auto" derives phi = 1/N_poles from conductor table (1.0 AC, 0.5 DC bipole)

  # Load-shed fraction (rho) — fraction of lost flow that becomes unserved energy
  # "auto" derives from AC/DC: AC meshed = 0.05, DC point-to-point = 0.80
  load_shed_fraction: "auto"

  # Redispatch cost ($/MWh) — congestion premium for rerouting power during outage
  # $/MWh, 2025$ (CPI-U from ~2021$, ×1.1880). LBNL Millstein et al. 2022, empirical congestion relief values.
  redispatch_cost_per_mwh: 24

  # Value of lost load (tiered by outage duration)
  # Piecewise VoLL: 10 tiers. Tiers 1-5 from Brattle/ERCOT 2024 system-wide survey (Table 13, 2024$).
  # Tiers 6-9 extrapolated via V(t) = 32210/t + 3339 + 492t ($/MWh), OLS fit to observed data.
  # Tier 10 is a flat cap at the 30-day extrapolated value.
  # ... 2025$ (CPI-U from 2024$, ×1.0262).
  value_of_lost_load:
    tiers:
      - max_hours: 1     # 0-1h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 36620 # $/MWh — ERCOT observed
      - max_hours: 2     # 1-2h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 21885 # $/MWh — ERCOT observed
      - max_hours: 4     # 2-4h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 13689 # $/MWh — ERCOT observed
      - max_hours: 8     # 4-8h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 10708 # $/MWh — ERCOT observed
      - max_hours: 16    # 8-16h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 13937 # $/MWh — ERCOT observed
      - max_hours: 32    # 16h-32h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 20628 # $/MWh — extrapolated
      - max_hours: 64    # 32h-64h (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 36282 # $/MWh — extrapolated
      - max_hours: 168   # 64h-7d (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 88512 # $/MWh — extrapolated
      - max_hours: 720   # 7d-30d (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 367280 # $/MWh — extrapolated
      - max_hours: .inf  # >30d — flat cap (>= 0)
        value_per_mwh: 367280 # $/MWh — capped at 30-day value

  # Base outage duration (hours per event) (>= 0)
  outage_duration: 6 # hours/event

  # Duration multiplier by construction type
  # H_eff = outage_duration × multiplier
  # All multipliers (>= 0)
  outage_duration_multiplier:
    overhead: 1.0 # (>= 0)
    underground: 80.0 # 6h × 80 = 480h (20 days) average XLPE land cable repair (CIGRE TB 815, 2020; Ofgem/GHD, 2020).
    subsea: 250.0 # 6h × 250 = 1500h (~62 days) effective subsea duration (CIGRE TB 815, IEA Wind TEM95, Leadvent; see docs/audits/2026-06-12__outage-parameter-sourcing.md)

  # Outage rates by construction type (line-level)
  # Overhead uses decomposition model: lambda = lambda_terminal + lambda_per_mile * L
  # Underground/subsea use pure per-mile rates (linear scaling confirmed by CIGRE/Ofgem data)
  outage_rate:
    overhead:
      lambda_terminal: 0.2136  # outages/yr (length-independent terminal/substation component). BC Hydro VITR EENS study (Appendix B, 230 kV overhead).
      lambda_per_mile: 0.012  # outages/mile/year (exposure-dependent). CEA 240kV 0.014, Zhou BPA 0.013, Poland 220kV 0.012.
    underground: 0.004  # outages/mile/year. CIGRE TB 379 (2009) / TB 815 (2020): land XLPE cable failure rate 0.002–0.005/cct-km (0.003–0.008/cct-mi); midpoint consistent with Ofgem/GHD (2020) UK cable data.
    subsea: 0.0007 # outages/mile/year. Ofgem/GHD (2020) total rate 0.000615/cct-km; ENTSO-E/Europacable (2019) 0.07 faults/100km/yr; CIGRE TB 815 (2020) confirms reduction from TB 379 levels.

14_category_om_structures.yaml.raw_content:
# Project Category O&M — Structures (Overhead) & Line O&M Rates (Non-Overhead)
#
# Overhead: flat base O&M rate per mile (excludes vegetation management, modeled separately in YAML 12).
# Non-overhead: total line O&M as % of line CAPEX per year (replaces conductor + structure decomposition).
# Line CAPEX = total build cost minus converter cost (conductor_cost + structure_cost from build costs module).

project_categories_om_structures:
  # OVERHEAD CONFIGURATIONS
  # Single base O&M rate per mile (excludes vegetation management, modeled separately in YAML 12).

  "Overhead":
    base_om_per_mile_year: 19090  # $/mile/year, 2025$. CT Siting Council (2022) $29,636/circuit-mile total (FERC Form 1, 2017–2021 mean, ~2019$) escalated to 2025$ at 2%/yr CAGR (×1.126 → $33,370) minus separately modeled vegetation management ($14,000 forested → $14,280 at 2025$). Covers conductor inspection, structure maintenance, patrol, and all non-VM line O&M.

  # NON-OVERHEAD CONFIGURATIONS
  # O&M as % of line CAPEX per year. Covers all non-converter maintenance:
  # cable monitoring, joint testing, civil infrastructure, surveys, repair provisioning.

  "Underground direct-buried":
    om_pct_of_line_capex: 0.0015  # 0.15% of line CAPEX/yr. Source: CIET/Powerlink (2023). Cross-check: CT Siting Council (2023) reports $22,937/circuit-mile from FERC Form 1 on $16–21M/mi CAPEX ≈ 0.11–0.14%.

  "Underground tunnel":
    om_pct_of_line_capex: 0.004   # 0.4% of line CAPEX/yr. Source: IET and Mott MacDonald (2025), "Electricity Transmission Costing Study," standard onshore O&M (SSM factor).

  "Subsea":
    om_pct_of_line_capex: 0.025   # 2.5% of cable system CAPEX/yr. Source: NeoMarketData (2025). Cross-check: Ofgem PCR data — Viking Link (2025), NSL (2023), IFA2 (2022) show 5.3–5.6% total system opex; cable-only portion ≈ 2.5%.

# Real O&M cost escalation (applies to all construction types, line + converter O&M)
om_real_escalation_rate: 0.02 # 2.0% real/yr. CT Siting Council (2022) official 40-yr lifecycle CAGR. Cross-check: LBNL FERC Form 1 data (2021) 0.5-2.0% real CAGR (117 IOUs); MCR Group/MISO (2024) 1.7% nominal.

# Cost Incurrence Timing for AFUDC Capitalization
# Defines when costs hit CWIP (Account 107) during project lifecycle
# Per FERC USoA: AFUDC applies when (i) capex incurred AND (ii) activities in progress

cost_timing_patterns:
  # Build costs (conductor, structure, converter)
  build_costs:
    during_delay: 0.0 # % of cost incurred during delay (typically 0)
    during_construction: 1.0 # % spread uniformly over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Qualifies for AFUDC (in CWIP Account 107)

  # ROW acquisition costs
  row_acquisition:
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 1.0
    afudc_eligible: true

  # ROW holding costs (annual cost during delay)
  row_holding:
    during_delay: 1.0 # Holding costs occur only during delay period
    during_construction: 0.0 # No holding costs once construction starts
    afudc_eligible: false # Operating expense, not capitalized to CWIP

  # ROW rent costs (annual cost during operation)
  row_rent:
    during_delay: 0.0 # No rent during delay
    during_construction: 0.0 # No rent during construction
    afudc_eligible: false # Operational expense, not in CWIP

  # Environmental mitigation - base restoration
  environmental_mitigation_base:
    during_delay: 0.0 # Restoration happens during construction
    during_construction: 1.0 # Spread over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Necessary for plant to be ready for service

  # Environmental mitigation - credit purchases
  environmental_mitigation_credits:
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 1.0
    afudc_eligible: true

  # Delay costs (regulatory/legal expenses)
  delay_costs:
    during_delay: 1.0 # By definition, occur during delay period
    during_construction: 0.0
    afudc_eligible: false # Typically expensed, not capitalized

  # O&M costs (operational period)
  operations_and_maintenance:
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 0.0 # O&M begins after COD
    afudc_eligible: false # Operating expenses

  # Insurance during construction
  construction_insurance: # THIS isnt not implemented yet but could be if I want to
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 1.0 # Spread over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Part of construction cost (can be capitalized)

# Construction spending profiles (S-curve)
# Year-by-year disbursement weights for how construction costs are spent across
# the construction period. Used for year-by-year AFUDC compounding.
#
# Source: MISO, Transmission Cost Estimation Guide for MTEP25, Table 5-1.
# URL: https://cdn.misoenergy.org/MISO%20Transmission%20Cost%20Estimation%20Guide%20for%20MTEP25337433.pdf

# These 4 reference profiles are pooled into a normalized cumulative S-curve
# and resampled to fit any construction_years value (see financial_utils.py).
# Delay-period spending uses uniform distribution (not S-curve).
